### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0dd5db2fc95b1aa7db36f2dc68351d17e48c0632` — the merge of head `c769a547bca53b06f472cfe4fcfd75fe5b2c4876` into base `82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0dd5db2fc95b1aa7db36f2dc68351d17e48c0632 && git checkout 0dd5db2fc95b1aa7db36f2dc68351d17e48c0632
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2 c769a547bca53b06f472cfe4fcfd75fe5b2c4876 && git checkout -B drift-repro 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2 && git merge --no-ff c769a547bca53b06f472cfe4fcfd75fe5b2c4876

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82a3ed2e861d260fdd65517e6b17f03c42eb90c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## ACCEPT · PR #31702 · #31630 · 2026-11-08T23:18Z

Head-sha: `a2ffc1687defa450f8c38c88224a23ff982773a3`

- **Seat review (TIER_DEFAULT; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; no contract face is hit, so no contract-review record is owed):** `RecycleBinWrittenEntry.withdraw()` removes the entry when the driver answers that the by-id delete removed nothing (`false`, or an off-contract `0`). It uses the unit's own driver options, so it runs inside the covering transaction when there is one. It shares `compensate`'s removal path, never throws, and logs a failed removal at `error` without changing the delete's answer. `recycleBinEntryId` is still told only for a removed row. Snapshot, restore and purge are untouched. Writing the entry before the removal is kept on purpose: a write after a non-transactional removal could leave a removed row with no undo. Right.
- **Open question** (os-dev-report on #31630): the root answers `false` after an atomic cascade has already removed its children. Ruled **A, keep**: the entry is withdrawn as the card's acceptance asks. Accepted deviation: in that race the cascaded children have no bin entry to restore from. The race is rare and needs a concurrent delete of the same root. No follow-up card.
- **Cascade-set path:** not the same shape (children open no capture), left unchanged, as the delta allows.
- **Surface:** claim on #31630 (`packages/objectql/src/**`) covers every file in the diff.
- **Tests and ablation:** 6 new pins in `capture.test.ts`; removing the `withdraw` call turns 5 red, restored. After the merge round on this head: objectql 11622, driver-memory 1772, dogfood recycle-bin files 148, objectql typecheck 0.
- **Prose face (TIER_DEFAULT):** the changeset's sentences match the diff: entry written before removal; withdrawn in the same unit on `false`/`0`; one entry and an unchanged `recycleBinEntryId` on a confirmed delete; snapshot, restore and purge untouched; a failed withdrawal logged at `error`.
- **Gates on this head:** CI attempt 1 had one red, `Test Core (7/8)`, on `plugin-security` `delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts`. That is the known timeout carded as #31663, in a package this diff does not touch (flake reading 6728293512). The failed jobs were re-run once through `run_rerun_failed` and passed. Every check-run on this head is now success (35) or skipped (15). `check-governed-merges --pr 31702`: not governed, +128/-23 (Tier S). K = 4 (< 15), `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Landing:** `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` in this stroke. Card closes on merge (`Fixes #31630`).

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [42536035987](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42536035987) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (7/8)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42536035987/job/128900969406)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```
  @objectstack/plugin-security:test:  FAIL  src/delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts > [ADR-0090 D12] a delegated answer about a user the caller cannot read does not depend on that user's existe
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/plugin-security:test: Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

**跨 PR 相同签名（24h，按失败测试文件聚合）：**

- `src/delegated-admin-own-name-set.posture.test.ts` — 24h 内已弹出 **2 个互相独立的 PR**（#31665、#31702）。汇总 issue：#31726（新建）
- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。

**历史信号：**
- 本 PR 过去 24h 无队列失败记录（首次）。
- 过去 24h 队列共有 13 个失败构建（不含本次）。

**分诊清单：**
1. 失败测试在本 PR 改动的包里 → 真回归，修 PR。
2. 失败测试与本 PR 无关 → 看上面的「跨 PR 相同签名」；已有汇总 issue ⇒ flaky/环境问题实锤，去那张 issue 上谈，修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列。
3. 两者都不是 → 可能与同组 PR 语义冲突；等前面的 PR 落地或失败出队后再重排一次即可，不要连续重排。
